The chapter in sum: the Amalekites spoiled the city and took the families while the men were gone up with Achish; David sought the Lord first, was told to pursue and recover, and went down and recovered all; and when his men that fought did not want to share with the men that were too faint, David made everybody part alike.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: The spoil went to them in Bethel, in south Ramoth, in Jattir, in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa, in Rachal, in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, in the cities of the Kenites, in Hormah, in Chorashan, in Athach, in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and abode two days in Ziklag, a man came out of the camp of Israel with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and fell to the earth before David to do him honor.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David asked him how the matter went, and he answered that the people were fled from the battle, many had fallen and were dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son were dead also.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David asked the man how he was not afraid to stretch forth his hand to destroy the Lord's anointed. Even a man about to die was not to be touched; the judgment of the Lord was to be let play out. David then commanded one of his young men to fall upon the Amalekite, and he died, for his own mouth had testified against him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David inquired of the Lord whether he should go up into any of the cities of Judah, and the Lord said, Go up, unto Hebron. David did not move to take the kingdom until he asked whether it was time to be king.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: David went up with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and with every man and his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: The men of Judah came and there anointed David king over the house of Judah. He was raised up because the Most High had anointed him to be the next king over Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: David sent to the men of Jabeshgilead who had buried Saul, blessing them for the kindness shown to their lord, and telling them Judah had anointed him king over them.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and made him king over Gilead and Israel; Ishbosheth was forty years old and reigned two years, while Judah followed David. David reigned in Hebron over Judah seven years and six months.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner and his men walked all that night and came to Mahanaim. Of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel were missing, but they had smitten of Abner's men three hundred and threescore. They buried Asahel at Bethlehem, and Joab and his men came to Hebron at break of day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: There was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David, but David waxed stronger and stronger and the house of Saul weaker and weaker. Each had those that followed him, but the Most High increased David because he had been anointed to be the next king over Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul. When Ishbosheth charged him over Rizpah, Saul's concubine, Abner was very wroth, saying he had shown kindness to the house of Saul and not delivered them to David, and now was charged with a fault concerning this woman.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner swore to do to himself and more, to translate the kingdom from the house of Saul and set up the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba. Ishbosheth could not answer him a word, because he feared him. Abner was through with Ishbosheth and turned to go with David and the Lord.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner sent messengers to David offering to bring all Israel to him. David agreed to make a league, but required that Michal, Saul's daughter, first be brought to him, and he sent to Ishbosheth to deliver his wife whom he had espoused for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner spoke with the elders of Israel and with Benjamin, reminding them they had sought David in times past, and that the Lord had said by the hand of David He would save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines and all their enemies. Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made them a feast, and Abner went in peace to gather all Israel to David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When David heard it, he declared himself and his kingdom guiltless before the Lord forever from the blood of Abner, and laid it on the head of Joab and all his father's house. He commanded Joab and all the people to rend their clothes and gird with sackcloth and mourn before Abner, and the king himself followed the coffin.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Rechab and Baanah escaped, having smitten and slain him on his bed; and they beheaded him and took his head and got away through the plain all night, and brought the head to David at Hebron, saying, Behold the head of Ishbosheth thine enemy, and claiming the Lord had avenged the king this day of Saul and his seed.
They did too much; they went overboard. Israel being out of order took the matter upon themselves. David had no quarrel with Saul's sons; it was Saul who sought his life.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: David answered Rechab and Baanah that as the Lord liveth, who had redeemed his soul out of all adversity, the man who told him Saul was dead, thinking to bring good tidings, he had taken hold of and slain in Ziklag; that was the reward he gave for such tidings.

This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart. He did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide; he called them out and they received judgment for taking a man's life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: David commanded his young men, and they slew Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron, but took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner. The Most High has His own way of doing things; His people are not to put the cart before the horse.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: David was anointed in Bethlehem, then over Judah in Hebron, and then over all twelve tribes. He reigned seven and a half years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: All the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron and said, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh, meaning we are kinsmen, related to thee.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: The elders of Israel came to Hebron, and David made a league with them before the Lord, and they anointed David king over Israel. This is when David was officially anointed king over all the nation.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: The Jebusites, inhabitants of the land, thought to put a stipulation on David that he could not come in unless he took away the blind and the lame, thinking he could not come in at all. They did not reckon with a man who had already slain his tens of thousands.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David. When the scripture says nevertheless, it means the thing will be done regardless of what stands against it.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David said that whosoever smote the Jebusites should be chief and captain. This was the type of warrior David was: a man after God's own heart, who would not let any nation stand in the way of the Lord's people.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David dwelt in the fort and grew great, and the Lord God of hosts was with him. The Most High was always with David, in the wars he fought and in the ones to come.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons, and they built David a house. Hiram was a man of Tyre, and this league would later serve to build the temple in Solomon's day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David perceived that the Lord had established him king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for His people Israel's sake.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David took more concubines and wives, and more sons and daughters were born to him in Jerusalem. That David had multiple wives does not make it right; the Most High forgave David many of his sins, but the brothers who teach a multiple-wives doctrine are not David and are not men after God's own heart. Not one of our forefathers besides Christ was without sin.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: When the Philistines heard David was anointed king, they came up to seek him, spreading themselves in the valley of Rephaim. They had already lost their champion Goliath, yet they came again to challenge this man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David inquired of the Lord, Shall I go up to the Philistines? Wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? He did not go to war on his own strength; he sought counsel first, for he knew where his power lay. The Lord answered that He would doubtless deliver them into David's hand.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David came to Baalperazim and smote them, and said the Lord had broken forth upon his enemies as a breach of waters. The victory was the Lord's, for the Lord is a man of war.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: When David inquired this time, the Lord said, Thou shalt not go up, but fetch a compass behind them and come upon them over against the mulberry trees. This is war strategy given by the Lord: David sought counsel again rather than assume the last answer.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

points: David gathered together thirty thousand chosen men of Israel. Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines, but everyone in the body is important in some way; the members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David and all the people went from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David was displeased that the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah, and he was afraid of the Lord that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? David had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of Him and His judgments.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: When David heard the Lord had blessed the house of Obededom because of the ark, he went and brought up the ark to the city of David with gladness. When those that bore it had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod. He was happy and in the spirit, for the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people. Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David answered that he danced before the Lord who chose him before her father to be ruler over Israel, therefore he would play before the Lord, and would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants he would be had in honor.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: The Lord reminded David that He took him from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over His people Israel, and was with him whithersoever he went, cutting off all his enemies and making him a great name.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

points: Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and this vision. Then David went in and sat before the Lord and said, Who am I, O Lord God, and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

points: He asked that the Lord's name be magnified for ever, that men would say, The Lord of hosts is the God of Israel, and that the house of His servant David be established before Him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

points: David smote the Philistines and subdued them, taking Methegammah out of their hand, and smote Moab, measuring them with a line, casting them to the ground. Our forefather David was a mighty warrior, subduing two different nations, which nations do not usually do at once.

With two lines he measured Moab to death and with one full line to keep alive; the Moabites became David's servants and brought gifts. War was not about killing everyone, for the living become servants and pay tribute; the fear was put in the nations so they would not fight back.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: David smote Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates, taking a thousand chariots, seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen, houghing the chariot horses but reserving a hundred chariots.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David slew twenty and two thousand of them and put garrisons in Syria, and the Syrians became servants and brought gifts. The Lord preserved David whithersoever he went. David took the shields of gold and much brass and carried them to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: This is the making of allies: when a stronger king removes an enemy you could never beat, the wise thing is to ally with him. David's kingdom made allies, but not by serving their idols or giving sons and daughters in marriage; the alliances served needful things, as Hiram later helped build the temple.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer, he sent his son Joram to salute and bless David, because Hadadezer had had wars with Toi. Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and brass.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: David got a name when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the valley of salt, eighteen thousand men. He put garrisons throughout all Edom, and all they of Edom became David's servants, and the Lord preserved David whithersoever he went.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: David reigned over all Israel and executed judgment and justice unto all his people. This is the mark of a real king and ruler: to lead the people in true judgment according to the commandments.

The prayer of a servant is to one day have the spirit of King David, to lead brothers and sisters in justice and truth, and for all the brothers to become such leaders, each praying that those under them be better than themselves.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: David set his officers: Joab over the host; Jehoshaphat the recorder; Zadok and Ahimelech the priests; Seraiah the scribe; Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.

note.label: 2 Samuel 8: David Subdues the Nations

points: David asked whether there was yet any left of the house of Saul that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake. Remember that Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.
That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel; Jonathan was always there for David, that was David's homeboy, they were really close.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: The king sent and fetched him out of Lodebar. Because of the respect and love David had for Jonathan, David was going to show kindness to Jonathan's son, even though the son could not walk.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: To show his love for Jonathan, David gave everything that Saul owned to Jonathan's son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan came unto David he fell on his face and did reverence. David told him, Fear not, for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: The king of the children of Ammon died and Hanun his son reigned in his stead. David said he would show kindness unto Hanun as his father Nahash had shown kindness unto David, and sent his servants to comfort him for his father.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: The princes of Ammon told their lord Hanun that David had not sent comforters to honor his father, but had rather sent his servants to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it.

Through one generation to another they still had this beef with Israel; they kept it in their mind that these people were enemies, not meant to be at peace with them. So they put it in the king's mind that David was really coming to spy the land out and overthrow them.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: Hanun took David's servants, shaved off one half of their beards, cut off their garments in the middle even unto their buttocks, and sent them away. When it was told David, he sent to meet them because the men were greatly ashamed, telling them to tarry at Jericho until their beards be grown, then return.

One of the first things we learn coming into this truth is that a man has to have a beard and men have to pull up their pants. The beard is a badge of manly dignity, a law given by the Most High, and it is a shame for a man to shave it. These men were ashamed to come into the city with half a beard and their garments cut so their behind was showing; David did not even want them in the city until their beards grew back. That is what Israel has to change as a people; today men walk around with their behind showing as a fashion statement, but these men were greatly ashamed.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, they hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob and Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.

Once these men saw David did not like what happened, they knew David was a man of war and Israel a people of war, so they sought help. But David had already subdued these same nations; they simply tried to get the men who had always been beefing with Israel to come against Israel yet again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When the Syrians saw they were smitten before Israel, they gathered together, and Hadarezer sent for the Syrians beyond the river with Shobach the captain of the host. David gathered all Israel, passed over Jordan, and the Syrians fled before Israel. David slew the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen and smote Shobach, who died there.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: After the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, David sent Joab and all Israel to destroy the children of Ammon and besiege Rabbah, but David tarried still at Jerusalem. In the evening he walked upon the roof, saw a woman washing herself who was very beautiful, inquired and learned she was Bathsheba the wife of Uriah the Hittite, sent and took her, and lay with her; and she conceived and told David, I am with child.

Masons and people in these fraternities always run here to justify wrongdoing, saying David slept with Bathsheba and the Most High still forgave him. But you are not King David; David was a man like the rest of us, and he messed up, and this is the mess up. About ninety percent of them go right back to David and Bathsheba every time they want to justify some wrongdoing.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: David arose from off his bed, walked upon the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon. He saw her and sent to inquire after the woman: I have power, let me send some people over there.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: David walked on the roof and saw a woman washing herself, and she was very beautiful to look upon. He saw, inquired, and took, the same pattern as Shechem. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house for the rest of his days, though the Lord forgave him.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite? Somebody with a spiritual mind made it clear: this is somebody's wife. And David sent messengers, and took her anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he ignored them.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: And she came in unto him, and he lay with her. She was not right either: she did not resist, she was not opposed; she thought she came up. And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: David's plan, which nobody was privy to, was that if Uriah went down and slept with his wife, they could say the child was his. A lot of us do that today: many people raise children that are not theirs, and just because David did it does not make it right.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: David sent to Joab to send him Uriah. When Uriah came, David asked how Joab and the people did and how the war prospered, then told him to go down to his house and wash his feet, sending a mess of meat after him. But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house. When David heard it, he asked Uriah why he came not from his journey and went not down.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Uriah told David that the ark and Israel and Judah abode in tents, and Joab and the servants of his lord were encamped in the open fields; so how could he go into his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife? As David lived, he would not do this thing. David kept him another day and made him drunk, but that evening Uriah still went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Uriah had a sense of loyalty that was probably killing David all the more, because David could not deceive this man into laying with his wife. Even drunk, when a man might just go home to sleep it off, Uriah still slept at David's house and would not go down.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah, ordering that Uriah be set in the forefront of the hottest battle and then abandoned, that he might be smitten and die. Joab assigned Uriah to a place where he knew valiant men were, and when the men of the city fought, some of David's servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite died also.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Joab sent and told David all concerning the war, charging the messenger that if the king's wrath arose over drawing so nigh the city, he should then say that Uriah the Hittite was dead also. When the messenger delivered it, David told him to say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another; make the battle stronger and overthrow the city.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: When the wife of Uriah heard her husband was dead, she mourned for him, and when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house and she became his wife and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the Most High.

It displeased the Most High because it was murder; he set the man up to be murdered on a battlefield, which was not a righteous thing. Bathsheba was not innocent either; she was complicit. When David called for her she went, she did not refuse because she was married, and it was consensual, not rape. She knew she was pregnant, so this was deceitful on both sides.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Nathan came to David with a parable. When David judged that the man deserved to die for taking the poor man's one lamb, he was unknowingly pronouncing sentence on himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: The Lord sent Nathan unto David with the parable of the rich man who spared his own flock and took the poor man's one little ewe lamb. David's anger was greatly kindled: the man that hath done this thing shall surely die. And Nathan said, thou art the man. The rich man is you, David; the poor man was Uriah the Hittite, and the ewe lamb was his wife.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Nathan said unto David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Most High: I anointed thee king over Israel, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul, gave thee thy master's house and wives, and the house of Israel and of Judah, and would have given thee more. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment to do evil, killing Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taking his wife, slaying him with the sword of the children of Ammon?

The Most High said if David would have just asked, He would have given him anything, for He had already given him the kingdom, Saul's house, and protection from Saul. The commandment David despised was what was read in Deuteronomy 27. There is a term called suicide by cop; David committed murder by the hand of another nation, because he set the whole thing up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: Nathan had to approach David with a parable, because at this point David was out of his right mind; approach him the wrong way and he could have been killed too. Once the example gave David conviction, he came to his senses: I have sinned against the Lord.

The Lord said, what thou didst secretly, I will do this thing before all Israel: the sword shall never depart from thine house. And Nathan said, the Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. But evil stayed in David's house perpetually: the trouble among his sons, his own counsellor turning against him, being chased out of his kingdom. David was never the same after this.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The judgment of David was that child being put to death. This goes back to Exodus 34: the Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquities of the fathers upon the children. David got pardoned, but he did not get cleared; the punishment was still coming, one part the men of Israel dying in battle, the other his son having to die and his house having nothing but trouble.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: Nathan departed, and the Most High struck the child, so that it was very sick.
